# `silk/machine/simple`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The short form of a machine that has only states and events.

## When to use
Implement [`SimpleMachine`](#SimpleMachine) in place of `Machine` when a machine keeps no context and queues
no effects: a toggle, a traffic light, the steps of a form. It names one type, the events,
where `Machine` names three. Move to `Machine` when the machine needs data or effects.

## Details
`SimpleMachine<E>` is another name for `Machine<E, NoContext, NoEffect>`, so everything that
takes a machine takes a simple one: snapshots, actors, definitions, the xstate config and
paths. [`Simple`](#Simple) has the calls that would otherwise repeat those two types, and
[`Simple.chart`](#Simple.impl.chart) starts the chart:

```silk
import silk.machine.chart { Chart }
import silk.machine.simple { Simple, SimpleChart, SimpleMachine }

union Lamp {
  Off,
  On,
}

union LampEvent {
  Toggle,
}

impl SimpleMachine<LampEvent> for Lamp {
  static fn chart() -> SimpleChart<Lamp, LampEvent> {
    return Simple.chart<Lamp, LampEvent>()
      |> Chart.initial(Lamp.Off)
      |> Chart.on("Off", "Toggle", Lamp.On)
      |> Chart.on("On", "Toggle", Lamp.Off)
  }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Simple` with `import silk.machine.simple { Simple }`.

<a id="Simple.impl.play"></a>

### Associated function `play`

```silk
pub effect fn play<'env, S: SimpleMachine<E>, E: 'static, G, ? Q>(
    snapshot: &mut SimpleSnapshot<S, E>,
    sender: &Sender<Signal<E>>,
    inbox: &Receiver<Signal<E>>,
    watch: effect fn<'env>(&SimpleSnapshot<S, E>) -> () ! G ? Q,
  ) -> ()
    ! G | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError | TaskIdExhaustedError
    ? Q | &mut Allocator | &mut Scheduler | &mut SystemClock
```

Plays the machine on the real clock: it takes the events that arrive on `inbox` and the
delayed transitions when they are due, with no call to [`Simple.advance`](#Simple.impl.advance), until the
machine reaches a final state or a `Signal.Stop` arrives.

#### Details
`watch` gets the snapshot after each event and after each delayed transition, to draw or
print the new state. `sender` must send to the channel of `inbox`: the machine uses it to
wake itself up when a delay ends. Send `Signal.Event { event }` through a clone of it from
any other fiber. This is `Actors.drive` for a machine without effects.
